gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the AC idle draw of the DELTA Pro 3, F3800 or Explorer 5000 Plus. Counted over a freezer's 72 hours, that idle draw uses as much energy as the freezer or more (58 W × 72 h = 4.2 kWh against 3.0 kWh for the freezer), so none of ChatGPT's three picks lasts 3 days on battery alone at 1 kWh/day (about 1.1 to 1.8 days, not 3.3 to 4.3). A 400 W panel does not cover a day's use.
standout_why: I compared ChatGPT's answer and the Solar Waypoint F3800 vs DELTA Pro 3 vs 5000 Plus comparison, the only third-party result it got. Solar Waypoint has no idle or no-load figure for any of the three; when I read the page, every idle field came back 'not listed'. ChatGPT's runtimes (3.5, 3.3 and 4.3 days) come from capacity × 85% ÷ 1 kWh/day and ignore the inverter's fixed draw, which runs all 72 hours because a freezer needs AC the whole time. The cited EcoFlow and Anker pages give no idle figure either; on the Anker F3800 page I opened, the specs list none.
decides: This changes the answer. At ChatGPT's own 1 kWh/day freezer, none of its three picks reaches 3 days on battery alone once idle draw is counted, and the biggest battery doesn't win by much. The Jackery 5000 Plus at 58 W idle comes out at about 1.8 days, roughly the same as the DELTA Pro 3 at 40 to 50 W. Solar is needed, not optional. Using ChatGPT's own assumption of 4 sun-hours × 75%, breaking even takes about 700 to 1,000 W of panels, not 400 W. The page should rank on days = 0.85 × Wh ÷ (freezer Wh/day + idle W × 24) and favor stations with idle around 20 W. For scale, The Solar Lab measured 20.5 W on the Anker F3000, which costs 0.49 kWh/day against 1.4 kWh/day for the 5000 Plus.
